correctness.rationale: For 2<=r<=n-2 with connected sparse paving M, the canonical polytope is the rank-r hypersimplex with each circuit-hyperplane corner cut by x(H)<=r-1. Hypersimplex coordinate facets have Eulerian-number Euclidean volumes. The removed corner has new facet Delta(r,r-1) x Delta(n-r,1) of (n-2)-volume sqrt(r(n-r))/((r-1)!(n-r-1)!) and old facet losses r L_1+(n-r)L_0. Distinct circuit hyperplanes overlap in at most r-2 elements, so their strict removed corners and positive-area cut patches have disjoint relative interiors. Summing produces A=A_0-lambda D. D is strictly positive and symmetric; comparison of factorial denominators and the displayed inequalities proves strict increase toward middle rank. Verified n=5,6,7 Euclidean convex hulls independently in an orthonormal affine basis and coefficient inequalities for n=4..34, including the n=6 r=3 two-intersection-pattern example; these finite tests do not replace the all-n proof. Lower-dimensional disconnected exceptional cases are excluded.

originality.rationale: PASS with a substantial and explicit prior-coverage restriction. Ferroni and Schroeter (2024) Corollary 5.4 ALREADY proves that every valuative matroid invariant of sparse-paving matroids depends only on n,r and number of circuit-hyperplanes, hence already covers this invariance for the surface-area intrinsic volume. The surviving result is the *evaluated ordinary Euclidean* coefficient D(n,r) with its metric covolume factors, strict positivity and exact rankwise balanced extremum; those numerical/ordering assertions were not found in the relevant Corollary 5.4 or the face-vector paper. Do not credit circuit-hyperplane-count invariance as new.
